# Introduction

Scientific posters need flexible layouts: variable column counts, arbitrary
dimensions, institutional branding, and figures that can span the full poster
width. This extension provides all of that from plain Quarto markdown.

::: {.poster-box .highlight title="Key finding"}
Fenced divs become styled boxes. Use `.highlight` or `.alert` variants and an
optional `title` attribute.
:::

# Methods

Body text flows through the configured number of columns. Standard markdown
works: **bold**, *italic*, lists:

- Column count set in YAML (`poster.columns`)
- Poster size as `"48x36"` or named sizes (`a0`, `a1`, `a2`)
- Themes switchable per poster

## Subheading style

Level-2 headings get an underline treatment instead of a filled bar.

# Results

Force a column break anywhere:

::: {.col-break}
:::

Figures placed normally occupy their column. To span all columns, wrap in a
`.full-width` div:

::: {.full-width}
![A full-width figure spanning every column](logos/wide-figure.svg)
:::

More results text after the full-width figure continues flowing in columns as
expected.

# Conclusions

::: {.alert title="Take-home message"}
One extension, any poster size, any column count, any number of logos.
:::
